clue.text: Swam with fish in a sea

indicators.note: in tells us the fish goes inside the sea's letters

parts.note: the Red Sea gives RED
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A swimmer splashed about alongside fish out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swam' is not about swimming: one's head swims or reels when giddy.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swims you feel dizzy and stagger, the past tense of reel in its giddy sense.

clue.text: Rogue artist's style is detailed

parts.note: RA (Royal Academician) is an artist, plus S for the 's

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, losing its last letter

parts.note: to call someone something is to style or name them

explanation.surface: A villainous painter's manner is elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'intricate' but means de-tailed: CALL loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel or mischievous scamp is a synonym for rogue.

clue.text: Former support to include Queen's Treasury

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to include means the support word holds the abbreviation within

parts.note: to cheer someone on is to support them

explanation.surface: A former backer now takes in the Queen's Treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK government department in charge of public revenue, the national treasury.

clue.text: Sweetheart's suspicious catching betrayer's mistake

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: catching means the suspicious word traps the betrayer inside

parts.note: rum means odd or suspicious
a rat is a betrayer or informer

explanation.surface: A lover's dubious act of catching a traitor's error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is not a lover but the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed error, listed in an errata slip, is a mistake.

clue.text: Was keen to change small imperfection

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of the two words to be rearranged

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone was eager to correct a minor flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges WAS KEEN into WEAKNES; S for small completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw or failing in character is a synonym for an imperfection.

clue.text: Produce from European cow, perhaps

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, of which a cow is an example

explanation.surface: Something made from the milk of a continental cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says a cow is one kind of dam, a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cheese is dairy produce, an example of the category.

clue.text: Going after equipment, start to cook chicken here?

indicators.note: going after puts the rest following the word for equipment

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of cook

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Chasing after gear, you begin to cook chicken somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'here' the definition: the place where chicken is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where one cooks chicken is where 'here' points, a definition by example.

clue.text: Artist's apparatus left holding up edge

indicators.note: in a down clue holding up means the left letter sits beneath and supports the rest

parts.note: to edge forward is to ease slowly along

explanation.surface: A painter's kit, with something on the left propping up its side.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand that holds the canvas is a piece of artist's apparatus.

clue.text: Forbidding nun to keep fashionable

indicators.note: to keep means the nun word holds the fashionable word inside

parts.note: a nun is a sister
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A stern ban on nuns keeping up with fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb (banning) but is the adjective: grim and menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing and ominous, threatening in appearance, is the sense shared with forbidding.

clue.text: Rogue in court is confident

indicators.note: in places the rogue inside the court

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat, and the Holy See is the papal court
a cur is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain standing in the dock remains self-assured.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sure and untroubled, free of doubt, is the sense shared with confident.

clue.text: Biased worker follows quietly

indicators.note: follows puts the worker after the word for quietly

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A prejudiced employee trails along behind someone without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fiercely loyal to one side is one-sided, a synonym for biased.

clue.text: Mouth of a fast river

parts.note: pert has an old sense of brisk or quick, listed in Chambers
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The estuary of a swift-flowing river.
explanation.walkthrough: PERT for fast is an obscure dictionary sense (brisk); the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or gap, such as the mouth of a cave, is called an aperture.

clue.text: Arbitrary component of error and omission

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arbitrary choice as a part of mistakes and oversights.
explanation.definitionFit: Chosen by chance, without plan or reason, is what arbitrary means.

clue.text: Hard cases suffering on board ship

indicators.note: on board places the suffering inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
hell is torment or suffering

explanation.surface: Tough characters endure misery aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cases' looks like tough people; it means hard outer casings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts, eggs and molluscs have rigid outer coverings, protective casings that are hard.

clue.text: Material from The Yorkshire Post?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
to post a notice is to issue it

explanation.surface: Content taken from a regional newspaper, The Yorkshire Post.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper's name is split: 'The' as Yorkshire folk say it, T', and 'Post' meaning send out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine paper or a thin woven fabric is a material.

clue.text: Indecent playing alone in tub embracing blokes

indicators.note: embracing means the rearranged letters hold the blokes inside
playing suggests the words are messed about with into a new order

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Something rude about splashing around alone in the bath with men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges ALONE IN TUB into UNTIONABLE, which then wraps the blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too shocking or rude to be spoken of is indecent, an extension of meaning.

clue.text: Live around winter's end, a creature's living

indicators.note: around means the word for live goes round the letter picked

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of the word winter

parts.note: a thing can be a creature, as in 'poor thing'

explanation.surface: A creature survives the end of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes R, the last letter of 'winter', which 'around' puts inside BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing breath means still alive, so living is a synonym.

clue.text: Deny detective's restrained person detaining one

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, plus S for the 's

indicators.note: detaining means the reticent person holds the one inside

parts.note: a clam is someone tight-lipped and reticent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A detective's detainee refuses to admit anything while holding someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or repudiate a claim is to deny it.

clue.text: Thoughtless prisoner lies about pinching book

indicators.note: pinching means the shuffled letters grab the book and hold it inside
about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A careless inmate tells untruths after stealing a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges PRISONER LIES into IRRESPONSILE, and 'pinching' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without care for consequences, heedless, is what thoughtless conduct means.

clue.text: Disappoint somebody mad supporting son

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the mad person goes beneath the son

parts.note: 'mad as a hatter' makes a hatter someone mad

explanation.surface: A crazy figure propping up a son lets him down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash or crush someone's hopes is to disappoint them, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Stockade maybe is more exposed blocking raid, oddly

indicators.note: blocking means the exposed word surrounds and obstructs the letters picked

parts.note: barer means more bare or exposed

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word raid

explanation.surface: A fortified fence, made more vulnerable, is stopping a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is one kind of obstruction or fence, so 'maybe' marks an example.

clue.text: Get together a band for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means what is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a crew is a band or gang of people

explanation.surface: A group gathers to play to a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or collect over time is to gather, as interest builds up.

clue.text: Long garment about one's middle covering rear

indicators.note: covering means the first letters wrap around the word for rear

parts.note: CA (circa) is the Latin abbreviation for about
aft is the nautical word for at the rear

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Something long worn around the waist, hiding one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's middle' reads as a waist but means the middle letter of the word 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose ankle-length tunic worn in the Middle East is a long garment.

clue.text: Initially, first response usually isn't 'tomato'

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A quiz: what kind of thing is a tomato? People seldom answer correctly first time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a tomato is botanically a fruit, though most people first answer vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomato develops from a flower's ovary and holds seeds, so botanists class it in this category.

clue.text: Disturbed by new blue clothing United

indicators.note: clothing means the word for blue is wrapped around the United abbreviation

parts.note: blue means risqué or erotic
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Upset by a new blue football kit for United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is not a colour here but racy, and 'United' is a football club, the U of Man U.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and mentally unsettled is disturbed in the psychological sense.

clue.text: Love god is tender on rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sore means tender or painful

explanation.surface: Cupid's counterpart is feeling sensitive as he gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of desire, the equivalent of Cupid, is a love god.

clue.text: Strangely true, lady is cheating

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd confession: a woman is being unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital infidelity, being unfaithful to a spouse, is commonly called cheating.

clue.text: Drive's opening more frozen and more dangerous

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word drive

parts.note: icier means colder or more frozen

explanation.surface: A motorist's start is chillier and riskier.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicey means risky, so the comparative is riskier, more dangerous.

clue.text: Driver conversely first on second tee

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the next piece follows the previous ones

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second
tee is the name of the letter T
or introduces the alternative, much as conversely does
1ST is first, written with I standing for 1

explanation.surface: Reads as golf: a driver hit off the first tee, then the second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' and 'tee' suggest golf clubs, but the driver here is at a car's wheel. OR stands loosely for 'conversely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives a car is a driver, the everyday synonym.

clue.text: Capital's power remnant European Union rejected

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
a rag is a scrap or remnant of cloth

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: A capital city's power is a leftover that the EU has spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech Republic's seat of government, a capital city.
